references.text: Earlier in the story, the donkey sees the angel of the Lord for the first time and turns aside from the road, showing a pattern where the animal repeatedly sees what Balaam cannot see.
The donkey sees the angel again and presses Balaam's foot against the wall, and Balaam strikes her - this is the second of three events where the donkey reacts to the angel.
The angel of the Lord opens Balaam's eyes so that he finally sees the angel the donkey had seen all along.
The angel explains that the donkey turned aside because it saw the angel, and that by doing so it saved Balaam's life.
Peter refers to this event and describes how a mute donkey spoke with a human voice and stopped the prophet's madness.
The angel of the Lord reveals himself - a theme that recurs throughout the Old Testament when God intervenes in human situations.
Proverbs warns against uncontrolled anger, which is illustrated by Balaam's rage toward the donkey.
